subject: Authorization request: Rollback or traffic-shift for model-8eta p95 regression
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@finbridge.com>
Cc: ops@finbridge.com
Date: 2027-08-14 09:12:34 -0700
Subject: Authorization request: Rollback or traffic-shift for model-8eta p95 regression

Team / Sarah —

We surfaced a persistent p95 latency regression for model-8eta serving FinBridge traffic on the dedicated pool. Key facts:
- Detection window: 08:45–09:05 PDT spike, continuing through 09:10–09:00.
- Observed p95: baseline ~210ms -> current ~980ms (user-facing tail, verified across 3 regions for FinBridge route).
- Error rates remain low; failures are not increasing.
- Impact: FinBridge reports degraded UX for batched invoice-generations and live chat workflows (see attached p95_trend_model-8eta_20270814.png).

Immediate mitigation options (tradeoffs):
1) Roll back model-8eta -> model-8eta-stable (previous canonical variant). Restores latency historically, but requires governance approval to change pinned model version for FinBridge.
2) Traffic-shift 30% of FinBridge traffic to model-8delta (fallback variant) and observe canary for 30m. Lower risk, partial mitigation, may leave some users degraded.
3) Apply temporary traffic-cap at the edge to reduce tail (degrades throughput for large batches).

Requested action: I need explicit authorization from escalation owners to proceed with option #1 (rollback) or #2 (traffic-shift). FinBridge SLA p95 window requires a decision within 30 minutes to avoid a formal incident declaration. If you authorize rollback, Marcus — please stand by to run the rollback runbook (attached) once I confirm.

Attachments: rollback_runbook_model-8eta_v1.pdf, p95_trend_model-8eta_20270814.png

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Sarah Patel <sarah@finbridge.com>
Date: 2027-08-14 10:01:22 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization request: Rollback or traffic-shift for model-8eta p95 regression

On Thu, Aug 14, 2027 at 09:12 AM Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team / Sarah —
> 
> We surfaced a persistent p95 latency regression for model-8eta serving FinBridge traffic ...

Naomi — thanks for the rapid heads-up and the clear options. My preference is to avoid a full rollback unless we have high confidence the variant was the root cause. Let's do a controlled traffic-shift first:
- Move 30% traffic to model-8delta for 30 minutes (canary).
- Monitor p95, median, and queue depth; if p95 for the canary drops below 300ms and error rates <0.1% we escalate to 60% traffic shift.

If the canary fails (p95 > 400ms or error delta > 0.5%), authorize rollback to model-8eta-stable immediately.

Marcus — please prepare the canary routing command and ensure the rollback runbook is staged. Hannah — coordinate a brief customer note to FinBridge if we begin rollback.

I'll approve the traffic-shift now provided the runbook and monitoring are ready.

- Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Product Reliability, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
From: Sarah Patel <sarah@finbridge.com>

Date: 2027-08-14 11:05:12 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization request: Rollback or traffic-shift for model-8eta p95 regression

Thanks Naomi and Sean —

We appreciate the quick investigation. Two asks from FinBridge ops:
1) Please share the expected customer-facing message and ETA to full mitigation for our incident channel.
2) If you perform a rollback, will any inference schema or tokenization change? We need to confirm no downstream transformations will regress our pipelines.

If the canary improves performance quickly we prefer that to a rollback. If a rollback is necessary, we request a 15-minute heads-up before switching traffic.

— Sarah
Sarah Patel
Head of Platform Engineering, FinBridge
ops@finbridge.com
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Patel <sarah@finbridge.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finbridge.com
Date: 2027-08-14 13:05:55 -07:00
Subject: Re: Authorization request: Rollback or traffic-shift for model-8eta p95 regression

Decision and next steps: authorized traffic-shift -> conditional rollback

Per Sean's plan we initiated a 30% traffic-shift to model-8delta at 10:12 PDT. Early canary results:
- 10:12–10:42: canary p95 ~280ms, median stable, no error uptick.
- 10:45–11:15: sustained improvement for canary; at 11:20 we increased to 60%.
- 12:00–12:30: overall FinBridge p95 improved to ~320ms. However at 12:45 we observed renewed tail in the primary variant (model-8eta) when large batches hit their queue; regression persisted for certain batch sizes.

Because the regression is repeatable on large-batch routes, and the canary shows improved latency, we will proceed with an ordered plan:
1) Increase traffic shift to 80% (now) while we prepare rollback artifacts.
2) Marcus — stage the rollback runbook and hold for authorization window. If queue-depth-trigger OR p95(primary) > 700ms for 2 consecutive 5-minute windows after the 80% shift, I authorize an immediate rollback to model-8eta-stable.
3) Hannah — prep the customer-facing note (short incident bulletin) and post to FinBridge ops channel once rollback is scheduled.

Attachments: rollback_runbook_model-8eta_v1.pdf (internal runbook).

Thanks all — I'll keep the thread updated.

Naomi Feldman
Sr. Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
